transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Most of us now check our phones dozens of times a day, rarely stopping to ask why. The apps we use are engineered to hold our attention for as long as possible, because our attention is what advertisers are buying. Critics argue that this constant stimulation erodes our capacity for deep concentration. Defenders, however, point out that technology has also made information more accessible than ever before. Perhaps the real issue is not the devices themselves, but our reluctance to set boundaries around them. Unless we decide consciously how to spend our attention, someone else will decide for us.

reading.title: My Daily Routine
reading.body:
My name is Lena. I get up at seven o'clock. I have breakfast with my family. We eat bread and eggs, and I drink tea.

I go to work by bus. I start work at nine. At twelve, I eat lunch with my friends. I finish work at five.

In the evening, I cook dinner. After dinner, I read a book or watch TV. I go to bed at eleven.

reading.title: A Weekend in Edinburgh
reading.body:
Last month, my friend Tom and I spent a weekend in Edinburgh. We took an early train from London on Friday morning, and it took about four and a half hours.

On Saturday, we visited the castle, which stands on a hill in the middle of the city. The view was fantastic, but it was very windy! In the afternoon, we walked along the Royal Mile and bought some small presents for our families.

On Sunday, it rained, so we went to a museum and had lunch in a traditional pub. I tried haggis for the first time. It was better than I expected. We came home tired, but we both want to go back soon.

reading.title: The Rise of Remote Work
reading.body:
Over the past few years, working from home has changed from a rare privilege into an ordinary option for millions of employees. Companies have discovered that many tasks can be done just as well outside the office, and workers appreciate the time and money they save on travelling.

However, remote work is not without problems. Some employees report feeling isolated, because they rarely meet colleagues in person. Others find it difficult to separate work from private life, especially when their desk is in the living room.

As a result, many companies are now trying a hybrid model, in which staff work from home on some days and come to the office on others. Supporters say this combines the advantages of both worlds, although critics point out that it requires careful planning to work well.

reading.title: Why Sleep Matters
reading.body:
It is tempting to regard sleep as wasted time, particularly when deadlines are looming. Yet decades of research suggest that adequate sleep is anything but a luxury. During the night, the brain consolidates memories, clears away waste products and restores the emotional balance that makes difficult days bearable.

The consequences of chronic sleep deprivation are well documented. People who regularly sleep fewer than six hours are more likely to suffer from heart disease, to gain weight and to have difficulty concentrating. Perhaps more surprisingly, even a single poor night can impair judgement to a degree comparable with mild intoxication.

Experts therefore recommend keeping regular hours, avoiding screens before bed and limiting caffeine in the afternoon. Such measures sound unremarkable, but, when followed consistently, they can make a considerable difference to both health and productivity.

reading.title: The Case for Slow Learning
reading.body:
In an age that prizes speed, the idea of learning slowly can seem almost perverse. Language apps promise fluency in weeks, and productivity gurus insist that every spare minute should be optimised. Yet cognitive scientists have repeatedly shown that durable knowledge is rarely acquired in a hurry. Memories laid down through spaced, effortful practice persist far longer than those crammed the night before an examination.

This does not mean that progress should be leisurely for its own sake. Rather, it suggests that struggle is not a sign of failure but a condition of genuine learning. Learners who tolerate confusion, revisit difficult material and allow time between sessions tend to retain more, even if they feel less confident in the short term.

The implication is uncomfortable but liberating: there are no shortcuts, yet there is no need to panic either. Steady, deliberate practice, sustained over months, will outperform any frantic burst of effort.

speaking.prompt_tr: Örnek cümleleri dinle, sonra kendi bilgilerinle kendini tanıt.

I get up at seven. I have breakfast and drink tea. Then I take a shower and get dressed. I leave home at eight.

On the other hand, the summers are extremely crowded because of tourists, and housing has become quite expensive. Overall, I would recommend it for a short holiday, but I'm not sure everyone would enjoy living there.

writing.prompt_tr: Bugün seni zorlayan bir durumu ve onunla nasıl başa çıktığını günlüğüne yaz.
writing.sample_answer: Today was a tough day at work. At first, everything went wrong: my computer crashed and I lost an hour of work. I felt frustrated, but I took a short walk to calm down. In the end, I managed to finish the report before the deadline. I realised that panicking does not help; a clear head does.

writing.prompt_tr: “Herkes haftada en az iki gün evden çalışabilmeli.” görüşüne katılıp katılmadığını gerekçeleriyle yaz.
writing.sample_answer: In my view, employees should be able to work from home at least two days a week. For instance, people who live far from the office can save hours of travel and use that time more productively. Nevertheless, I believe that regular face-to-face meetings remain important, because they build trust and make collaboration easier. A flexible balance therefore seems the most sensible solution.

writing.prompt_tr: Sosyal medyanın demokratik tartışmayı güçlendirdiği mi yoksa zayıflattığı mı konusunda dengeli bir paragraf yaz.
writing.sample_answer: It could be argued that social media has both strengthened and weakened democratic debate. To a certain extent, it has given ordinary citizens a platform that was once reserved for journalists and politicians, allowing marginalised voices to be heard. By contrast, algorithms tend to reward outrage rather than nuance, which encourages polarisation and the spread of misinformation. Furthermore, people increasingly consume news that confirms what they already believe, so genuine disagreement becomes rare. The solution, therefore, is probably not to abandon these platforms but to demand greater transparency from the companies that run them and better media literacy from their users.

grammar.summary_tr:
“Olmak” fiili İngilizce’de özneye göre değişir:
• I → am
• he / she / it → is
• we / you / they → are

Olumsuz için fiilden sonra not eklenir: I am not, he is not (isn't), they are not (aren't). Soru için fiil özneden önce gelir: Are you ready?

examples.text: I am a teacher.
She is from Italy.
They are not at home.
Are you hungry?

practice_items.explain_tr: Soruda fiil başa gelir; they ile “are”.

grammar.summary_tr:
İngilizce’de isimlerin önünde artikel kullanılır.
• a / an → belirsiz, tek bir şey (“bir”). Sesli harfle başlayan sözcüklerde “an”: an apple, an hour. Diğerlerinde “a”: a book.
• the → belirli, hem konuşan hem dinleyen hangisinden söz edildiğini biliyor: the sun, the book on the table.
• İlk kez söz edince a/an, tekrar söz edince the: I have a dog. The dog is big.
• Çoğul ve sayılamayan isimlerde genel anlatımda artikel kullanılmaz: I like music.

examples.text: I have a cat and an umbrella.
examples.tr: Bir kedim ve bir şemsiyem var.

examples.text: The cat is under the table.
She is an engineer.
I like coffee.

practice_items.prompt: I saw a film yesterday. ___ film was great.
practice_items.explain_tr: Film daha önce söz edildiği için belirli: the.
“honest” sesli harfle (h okunmaz) başlar; an honest man.
Hangi pencere olduğu belli olduğunda “the” kullanılır.

grammar.summary_tr:
Alışkanlıklar, düzenli işler ve genel gerçekler için geniş zaman kullanılır.
• Olumlu: I/you/we/they + fiil; he/she/it + fiil+s → She works.
• Olumsuz: don’t / doesn’t + fiilin yalın hâli → He doesn’t work. (works değil!)
• Soru: Do / Does + özne + yalın fiil → Does she work here?
• Sık kullanılan zarflar: always, usually, often, sometimes, never; fiilden önce, “be”den sonra gelir.

examples.text: I drink tea every morning.
She works in a bank.
He doesn’t like fish.
Do you speak English?

grammar.summary_tr:
Bir şeyin var olduğunu söylemek için kullanılır (“…var”).
• There is + tekil veya sayılamayan: There is a park near here. There is some milk.
• There are + çoğul: There are two chairs.
• Olumsuz: There isn’t / There aren’t (any …).
• Soru: Is there …? / Are there …? Kısa cevap: Yes, there is. / No, there aren’t.
• Soruda ve olumsuzda “any” kullanılır: Are there any shops?

examples.text: There is a bank next to the school.
There are three books on the desk.
There isn’t any milk.
Is there a bus stop near here?
examples.tr: Buraya yakın otobüs durağı var mı?

practice_items.prompt: There ___ any water in the bottle.

grammar.summary_tr:
Geçmişte bitmiş eylemler için kullanılır.
• Düzenli fiiller: fiil + -ed (walk → walked)
• Düzensiz fiiller ezberlenir (go → went, have → had, see → saw)
• Olumsuz: did not (didn't) + fiilin yalın hali: I didn't go.
• Soru: Did + özne + yalın fiil? Did you go?

Zaman ifadeleri: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2019.

examples.text: We walked to school.
She went to Paris last year.
I didn't see him.
Did you enjoy the film?

practice_items.prompt: She ___ to the party last night.
practice_items.explain_tr: did not'tan sonra yalın fiil gelir.

grammar.summary_tr:
Şu anda olan veya bu günlerde süren eylemler için: am/is/are + fiil+ing.
• I am working. / She is reading. / They are playing.
• Olumsuz: I’m not, he isn’t, we aren’t + fiil-ing.
• Soru: Are you listening?
• Yakın planlı gelecek için de kullanılır: I’m meeting Ali tomorrow.
• Durum fiilleri (know, like, want, understand) genelde -ing almaz: I know him. (I’m knowing değil)
• Yazım: make → making, run → running.

examples.text: I am studying English now.
She is cooking dinner.
They aren’t watching TV.
We are meeting Anna on Friday.

practice_items.explain_tr: Şu an olan olay: is raining.

practice_items.prompt: He ___ not sleeping at the moment. (is/are)

grammar.title_tr: Karşılaştırma ve üstünlük (-er / more / the most)
grammar.summary_tr:
• Kısa sıfatlara -er eklenir: tall → taller than. Üstünlük için the + -est: the tallest.
• Uzun sıfatlarda more / the most: more expensive than, the most expensive.
• -y ile biten: easy → easier → the easiest. Tek heceli, sessiz-sesli-sessiz: big → bigger → the biggest.
• Düzensizler: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → farther → the farthest.
• Eşitlik: as … as → She is as tall as me.

examples.text: My bag is heavier than yours.
This is the most interesting book.
Today is better than yesterday.
He is as tall as his father.

practice_items.prompt: She is the ___ girl in the class. (tall)

grammar.title_target: Prepositions of time and place: in, on, at
grammar.summary_tr:
Zaman:
• at → saat ve belirli anlar: at 8 o’clock, at night, at the weekend
• on → günler ve tarihler: on Monday, on 5 May, on my birthday
• in → ay, mevsim, yıl, günün bölümleri: in July, in summer, in 2024, in the morning
Yer:
• at → nokta: at the bus stop, at home, at work
• on → yüzey: on the table, on the wall
• in → kapalı alan, şehir, ülke: in the room, in Istanbul, in Turkey

examples.text: The class starts at 9 o’clock.
My birthday is on 12 June.
We go skiing in winter.
The keys are on the table.

grammar.title_tr: Sayılabilir / sayılamayan isimler (much, many, a lot of)
grammar.summary_tr:
• Sayılabilir isimler birer birer sayılır: one apple, two apples. Çoğulları vardır.
• Sayılamayan isimler sayılmaz: water, milk, money, information, advice. Çoğulu yoktur ve tekil fiil alır: The information is useful.
• many + sayılabilir çoğul: How many books? / much + sayılamayan: How much water?
• a lot of / lots of her ikisiyle olumlu cümlede kullanılır.
• a few + sayılabilir (birkaç), a little + sayılamayan (biraz).

examples.text: How many students are there?
We don’t have much time.
I need a little sugar.
She has a lot of friends.

practice_items.prompt: There are only ___ chairs in the room.
Can I have ___ water, please? (a few/a little)

grammar.summary_tr:
• going to → önceden verilmiş karar/plan veya şu anki kanıta dayalı tahmin: I’m going to study medicine. Look at the clouds, it’s going to rain.
• will → konuşma anında verilen karar, söz, teklif, tahmin: I’ll help you. I think it will be sunny.
• will + yalın fiil; olumsuz: won’t. Soru: Will you come?
• Sözle verilen vaatlerde ve “I think / probably” sonrasında will kullanılır.

examples.text: I’m going to visit my aunt this weekend.
examples.tr: Bu hafta sonu teyzemi ziyaret edeceğim.

examples.text: The phone is ringing. I’ll answer it.
She will probably be late.
We won’t forget your birthday.

practice_items.prompt: “We have no milk.” – “OK, I ___ buy some.”

I think it ___ rain tomorrow. (will/won’t – olumlu)
He ___ going to start a new job in May. (is/are)

grammar.summary_tr:
Geçmişte başlayıp bugünle bağlantısı olan olaylar için: have/has + V3 (past participle).
• Deneyim: I have been to Italy. (Ne zaman olduğu söylenmez.)
• Sonucu şimdi görülen olay: I have lost my keys.
• Süren durum: She has lived here for five years / since 2019.
• for + süre, since + başlangıç noktası. ever, never, already, yet, just sık kullanılır.
• Belirli geçmiş zaman (yesterday, in 2010, last week) varsa past simple gerekir: I went there last week.

examples.text: I have visited Berlin twice.
She has lived here since 2020.
Have you ever eaten sushi?
They haven’t finished yet.

practice_items.prompt: We have lived here ___ ten years. (for/since)

grammar.title_tr: Zorunluluk ve tavsiye (must, have to, should)
grammar.title_target: Modal verbs: must, have to, should
grammar.summary_tr:
• must → konuşanın kendi hissettiği güçlü zorunluluk; have to → dış kurallardan gelen zorunluluk: I have to wear a uniform at work.
• mustn’t → yasak (yapma!): You mustn’t smoke here. 
• don’t have to → zorunlu değil (gerek yok): You don’t have to come.
• should / shouldn’t → tavsiye: You should see a doctor.
• Modallerden sonra fiil yalın gelir ve -s almaz: She must go. Soru/olumsuz için do kullanılmaz (should, must); have to için do/does gerekir.

examples.text: You must wear a seat belt.
I have to get up early tomorrow.
You don’t have to pay.
You should drink more water.

practice_items.prompt: Students ___ use phones in the exam. It is forbidden.
It’s Sunday. I ___ go to work.
You look tired. You ___ go to bed early. (should/must to)

grammar.summary_tr:
Eylemi yapan kişi önemsiz ya da bilinmiyorsa edilgen kullanılır: be + V3.
• Present: The room is cleaned every day.
• Past: The window was broken last night.
• Will: The report will be finished tomorrow.
• Yapanı belirtmek için by: The book was written by Orwell.
• Soru: Was the window broken? Olumsuz: It wasn’t found.
• Aktif → Pasif: Someone stole my bike. → My bike was stolen.

examples.text: English is spoken all over the world.
The museum was built in 1900.
The letters will be sent tomorrow.
This song was written by my brother.

grammar.summary_tr:
İsmi tanımlayan cümleciklerdir (“…olan”).
• who → kişiler: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
• which → nesneler: The book which I bought is great.
• that → hem kişi hem nesne için (günlük konuşmada sık): The film that we saw was funny.
• where → yer: This is the café where we met.
• Nesne konumundaki who/which/that atılabilir: The book (that) I bought…
• Özne konumunda atılamaz: The man who called you is here.

examples.text: The woman who works here is my aunt.
This is the phone which I lost.
That is the school where I studied.
The film that we watched was boring.

practice_items.prompt: The girl ___ is sitting there is my sister.
This is the town ___ I grew up.
The car ___ I bought is red. (who/which)
The man ___ called you is my boss. (who/where)

options: The book who I read is good.
The book which I read it is good.
The book that I read is good.
The book where I read is good.

grammar.summary_tr:
Gelecekte gerçekleşmesi mümkün durumlar için:
If + present simple, will + yalın fiil

If it rains, we will stay at home.

Dikkat: “if” bölümünde will kullanılmaz. Sıralama değişebilir: We will stay at home if it rains (virgül gerekmez).

examples.text: If you study, you will pass the exam.
examples.highlight: If you study, you will pass

examples.text: If it rains, we will stay at home.
examples.highlight: If it rains, we will stay

examples.text: She will be happy if you call her.
examples.highlight: will be happy if you call

grammar.title_tr: İkinci tür koşul (If I were …, I would …)
grammar.summary_tr:
Gerçek dışı veya olası olmayan şimdiki/gelecek durumlar için:
• If + past simple, would + yalın fiil → If I had more money, I would travel the world.
• “be” fiilinde tüm özneler için “were” kullanılabilir: If I were you, I would call him.
• would yerine could / might da kullanılabilir.
• Gerçekleşmesi olası durumlar için first conditional: If it rains, I will stay home.

examples.text: If I won the lottery, I would buy a house.
If I were you, I would accept the job.
examples.tr: Senin yerinde olsam işi kabul ederdim.

examples.text: She would help us if she had time.
What would you do if you lost your passport?

grammar.summary_tr:
Başkasının sözünü aktarırken fiil genellikle bir adım geriye gider (backshift):
• am/is/are → was/were; present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous
• present perfect / past simple → past perfect; will → would; can → could
• Zamir ve zaman ifadeleri değişir: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, now → then, here → there.
• said / told: He said that… ; He told me that… (told + kişi).
• Sorular: dolaylıda düz cümle sırası kullanılır: She asked where I lived. Evet/hayır sorularında if/whether: He asked if I was ready.

examples.text: She said that she was tired.
He told me that he would call me.
They said they had finished.
He asked me where I lived.

grammar.summary_tr:
Geçmişteki bir olaydan daha önce olmuş başka bir olayı anlatır: had + V3.
• When I arrived, the film had already started. (Önce film başladı, sonra ben geldim.)
• Genellikle past simple ile birlikte: after, before, when, by the time, already, just.
• Olumsuz: hadn’t + V3. Soru: Had you finished…?
• Reported speech’te present perfect ve past simple’ın geri adımı: “I have seen it.” → He said he had seen it.

examples.text: When we arrived, the train had left.
She was tired because she hadn’t slept.
I had never seen snow before I moved to Canada.
examples.tr: Kanada’ya taşınmadan önce hiç kar görmemiştim.

examples.text: After he had eaten, he went to bed.

grammar.title_tr: Üçüncü tür koşul (If I had …, I would have …)
grammar.summary_tr:
Geçmişte gerçekleşmemiş durumlar ve hayali sonuçları için (pişmanlık, “…olsaydı … olurdu”):
• If + past perfect, would have + V3 → If I had studied, I would have passed.
• would yerine could have / might have da kullanılabilir.
• Olumsuz: If I hadn’t missed the bus, I wouldn’t have been late.
• Koşul ve sonuç yer değiştirebilir: I would have called you if I had known.

examples.text: If I had known, I would have helped you.
If she hadn’t been late, she would have caught the train.
We would have won if we had played better.
What would you have done if you had missed your flight?

grammar.title_tr: Devrik yapı (Never have I…, Rarely does…)
grammar.summary_tr:
Olumsuz veya kısıtlayıcı bir zarf cümlenin başına geldiğinde yardımcı fiil özneden önce gelir (soru düzeni gibi). Vurgu ve resmî üslup içindir.
• Never / Rarely / Seldom / Hardly / Scarcely / Not only / Under no circumstances / Only when / No sooner …
• Never have I seen such a view. · Rarely does she complain.
• Hardly had we sat down when the phone rang. (had + özne + V3 … when)
• No sooner had he left than it started to rain. (…than)
• Not only did he forget the tickets, but he also lost his passport.
• Yardımcı fiil yoksa do/does/did eklenir.

examples.text: Never have I seen such a beautiful view.
examples.tr: Hiç böylesine güzel bir manzara görmedim.

examples.text: Rarely does she complain about work.

grammar.title_tr: Karma koşul, wish ve if only
grammar.title_target: Mixed conditionals; wish and if only
grammar.summary_tr:
• Karma koşul (geçmiş → şimdi): If I had taken that job, I would be living in Berlin now.
• Karma koşul (şimdi → geçmiş): If she weren’t so shy, she would have asked for help.
• wish + past simple → şimdiki durumdan pişmanlık: I wish I had more time. (I wish I were taller.)
• wish + past perfect → geçmişten pişmanlık: I wish I had studied medicine.
• wish + would → başkasının alışkanlığından rahatsızlık: I wish you would stop interrupting.
• If only, wish ile aynı çalışır ama daha güçlüdür: If only he would listen!

examples.text: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Berlin now.
examples.tr: O işi kabul etseydim şimdi Berlin’de yaşıyor olurdum.

examples.text: If she weren’t so shy, she would have asked for help.

grammar.title_tr: Vurgu cümleleri (It was … who, What I need is …)
grammar.summary_tr:
Bir öğeyi öne çıkarmak için cümle ikiye bölünür.
• It-cleft: It + be + vurgulanan öğe + who/that … → It was Maria who solved the problem. It is consistency that matters most.
• Kişiler için who veya that, diğerleri için that: It was in Paris that they met.
• Wh-cleft: What + özne + fiil + be + vurgulanan öğe → What I need is a long holiday. What annoys me is the noise.
• All / The only thing: All she wanted was some peace and quiet.
• Vurgulu ve yazılı üslupta sık kullanılır.

examples.text: It was Maria who solved the problem.
It is consistency that matters most.
What I need is a long holiday.

grammar.summary_tr:
Özneleri aynı olan iki eylemi kısaltmak için kullanılır; yazılı üslupta sıktır.
• -ing (eş zamanlı, etken): Walking home, I met an old friend.
• Having + V3 (önce biten eylem): Having finished the report, she went home.
• V3 (edilgen): Written in 1925, the novel is still popular.
• Olumsuz: Not knowing the answer, he stayed silent.
• Ortacın örtük öznesi ana cümlenin öznesidir: Walking home, the rain started ✗ (yağmur yürümüyor).

examples.text: Walking home, I bumped into an old friend.
examples.tr: Eve yürürken eski bir arkadaşa rastladım.

examples.text: Having finished the report, she went home.
